To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) 3He proportional counters have an excellent response to neutrons with a peak efficiency of 40.3 +/- 1.2% for 1.8 MeV neutrons and a 1.5 MeV neutron detection threshold; (2) the response of the SNO detector to neutrons is well modeled by a Monte Carlo simulation; (3) 3He counters have an excellent low energy beta and gamma response with 1.5% energy resolution at

the 3He detector array in SNO has a 3.4 +/- 0.2 % efficiency for detecting neutrons produced in photodisintegration reactions and that the Cherenkov light background is dominated by the 40K decay chain, and can be reduced by 50% through the use of an external magnetic field.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how the SNO detector responds to the neutrinos that it was designed to detect.
the calibration of the SNO heavy water detector, which was designed to measure the flux of solar neutrinos through the charged current reaction on deuterium.
the calibration of the Sudury Neutrino Observatory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the calibration of SNO is complete, accurate, and reliable.
the 3He detector array is a highly effective detector for the detection of neutron events.
the SNO detector is working well and that the detector is ready for the science run.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated that SNO is capable of detecting and discriminating neutrons from gammas and electrons with an efficiency of 99.9% and a purity of 99.99%, and the ability to measure the neutron energy with an energy resolution of 5.2%.
the SNO detector is well understood and the response of the 1.5 ton heavy water target to the solar neutrino flux has been determined.
the calibration of SNO was achieved to an accuracy of better than 5%.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SNO detector is capable of measuring the flux of neutrinos in the range of 5 to 20 MeV with an accuracy of 5-10%.
the 3He counter array is very efficient at detecting low energy neutrons, and that the Cherenkov light produced in the heavy water is a significant source of background.
the SNO 3He detector is very sensitive to neutrons and can be used to detect neutrons with an efficiency of ~ 100% in the 1-3 MeV range.
